name: Car insurance
intro: The three cover levels sound like a ladder of price, but the middle option covers less than most drivers expect. Here's what each actually includes.

glossary.def: The amount you pay towards a claim before your insurer pays the rest. 'Compulsory' excess is set by the insurer; 'voluntary' excess is extra you choose to lower your premium.
A discount that grows for each claim-free year, and can usually be 'protected' for a fee so one claim doesn't reset it to zero.
Insurance Product Information Document — a short, standardised summary every UK insurer must give you before you buy, listing what's covered and what's excluded.
The legal minimum: covers injury or damage you cause to other people and their property, but nothing of your own.

head: Covers…
Third party only
Third party, fire & theft
Comprehensive
rows: Your car after an accident (any fault)

checklist: Add compulsory + voluntary excess together — that's what you'd actually pay per claim.
Check whether NCD protection is included or an extra cost, and what it actually protects.
Confirm your annual mileage estimate is realistic — insurers can reduce payouts if it's under-declared.
Declare every modification, even cosmetic ones — undeclared mods can void a claim.
If a telematics/black-box policy, check the curfew and driving-score rules before you agree to one.
